subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The opposition alliance that launched a movement against the results of the 1977 elections was the:
o: Movement for the Restoration of Democracy
explanation: The nine-party PNA alleged rigging in the March 1977 elections, and its agitation preceded Zia's coup.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: General Zia-ul-Haq's takeover of 5 July 1977 was code-named:
explanation: Zia overthrew Bhutto's government in Operation Fair Play and promised elections within ninety days.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was hanged in 1979 after being convicted in the murder case of:
explanation: Bhutto was convicted of conspiring to murder Nawab Muhammad Ahmad Khan Kasuri, father of Ahmed Raza Kasuri.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In March 2024, the Supreme Court gave its opinion in a presidential reference that Zulfikar Ali Bhutto:
o: Had not received a fair trial
explanation: The Court unanimously opined that the trial and appeal in Bhutto's case did not meet the requirements of a fair trial and due process.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Hudood Ordinances were promulgated in 1979 by:
explanation: Zia introduced the Hudood Ordinances as part of his Islamisation programme.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Protection of Women (Criminal Laws Amendment) Act 2006 amended:
explanation: The 2006 Act moved rape from the Zina Ordinance to the Pakistan Penal Code, removing the harsh evidentiary requirements of the Hudood laws.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, which introduced state deduction of Zakat from bank accounts, was issued in:
explanation: Zia's government promulgated the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance in 1980 as part of Islamisation.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The nominated advisory body set up by Zia-ul-Haq in the early 1980s in place of Parliament was called:
explanation: Zia's Federal Council (Majlis-e-Shoora) was nominated, not elected, and served in an advisory role until the 1985 elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The opposition alliance formed in 1981 to demand an end to Zia's martial law was the:
o: Movement for the Restoration of Democracy
explanation: The PPP-led MRD campaigned for elections and the restoration of the 1973 Constitution; its 1983 agitation was strongest in Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Zia-ul-Haq extended his presidency through a referendum held in:
explanation: The December 1984 referendum on Islamisation was treated as a mandate for Zia to remain President for five more years.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The general elections of 1985 were held on a:
o: Separate electorate basis only in Punjab
explanation: Zia held the 1985 elections without political parties; candidates stood as individuals.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Zia-ul-Haq's martial law was lifted in:
explanation: Martial law ended on 30 December 1985, after the Eighth Amendment had protected its actions.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first government dismissed under Article 58(2)(b) was that of Prime Minister:
explanation: Zia dismissed Junejo's government in May 1988, three years after it had been formed.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: General Zia-ul-Haq died in an air crash in August 1988 near:
explanation: Zia's C-130 crashed soon after take-off from Bahawalpur on 17 August 1988.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister for the first time in:
explanation: After the PPP emerged as the largest party in the November 1988 elections, Benazir was sworn in on 2 December 1988.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which President dismissed the governments of both Benazir Bhutto (1990) and Nawaz Sharif (1993)?
explanation: Ghulam Ishaq Khan used Article 58(2)(b) against Benazir in 1990 and Nawaz Sharif in 1993.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Nawaz Sharif first became Prime Minister in:
explanation: Nawaz Sharif led the IJI to victory in the 1990 elections and became Prime Minister in November 1990.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In 1993, the Supreme Court restored the National Assembly and the government of:
explanation: The Court held Ghulam Ishaq Khan's dissolution unlawful, but the resulting deadlock forced both President and Prime Minister to resign.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 1993 arrangement under which both the President and Prime Minister resigned was brokered by army chief:
explanation: The "Kakar formula" ended the standoff between Ghulam Ishaq Khan and Nawaz Sharif and led to fresh elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Moeenuddin Qureshi served as:
o: Governor of the State Bank in 1999
explanation: A former World Bank official, Moeen Qureshi led the caretaker government before the 1993 elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Benazir Bhutto's second government was dismissed in 1996 by President:
explanation: Farooq Leghari, himself a PPP leader, dismissed Benazir's government in November 1996 under Article 58(2)(b).

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Islami Jamhoori Ittehad (IJI), formed before the 1988 elections, was an alliance mainly opposed to the:
explanation: The IJI grouped the Muslim League, Jamaat-e-Islami and others against the PPP; Nawaz Sharif led it to power in 1990.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the 1997 general elections, the PML-N:
o: Won a two-thirds majority in the National Assembly
Lost to the PPP by a narrow margin
Formed a coalition with the PPP
explanation: Nawaz Sharif's heavy majority in 1997 enabled him to pass the 13th and 14th Amendments quickly.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: President Farooq Leghari resigned in December 1997 after a confrontation between the Nawaz Sharif government and Chief Justice:
explanation: Leghari sided with Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah in his clash with the government and resigned when the crisis turned against them; Rafiq Tarar succeeded him.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: General Pervez Musharraf removed Nawaz Sharif's government on:
explanation: The army took over after Nawaz Sharif tried to replace Musharraf as army chief while he was abroad.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After the coup of October 1999, Pervez Musharraf initially took the title of:
explanation: Musharraf avoided declaring formal martial law and called himself Chief Executive; he became President in 2001.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the Zafar Ali Shah case (2000), the Supreme Court validated Musharraf's takeover but directed that elections be held within:
explanation: The Court applied the doctrine of necessity and gave the regime three years to restore democracy, leading to the 2002 elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Musharraf's Devolution of Power Plan (2000–01) introduced elected local governments headed by:
explanation: The 2001 local government system created elected district, tehsil and union councils headed by nazims.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Whom did Pervez Musharraf replace as President in June 2001?
explanation: Musharraf assumed the presidency in June 2001, ending Rafiq Tarar's term early.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pervez Musharraf sought a five-year presidential mandate through a referendum held in:
explanation: The April 2002 referendum extended Musharraf's presidency, before the October 2002 general elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who became Prime Minister after the 2002 general elections?
explanation: Mir Zafarullah Khan Jamali of the PML-Q became Prime Minister in November 2002 and was the first from Balochistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who served as Prime Minister for about two months in 2004, between Zafarullah Khan Jamali and Shaukat Aziz?
explanation: After Jamali resigned in June 2004, PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain held office until Shaukat Aziz could enter the National Assembly.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which former Finance Minister served as Prime Minister from 2004 to 2007?
explanation: Shaukat Aziz replaced Jamali in 2004 and completed the Assembly's term in 2007.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lawyers' Movement of 2007 began after the suspension of Chief Justice:
explanation: Musharraf's attempt to remove Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry in March 2007 sparked a nationwide movement for judicial independence.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pervez Musharraf's conviction for high treason by a special court in 2019 related to his:
o: Imposition of emergency and suspension of the Constitution on 3 November 2007
explanation: The treason case concerned the November 2007 emergency; the 1999 coup had been validated by the courts and Parliament.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Charter of Democracy (2006) was signed by:
explanation: The two exiled leaders signed the Charter in London, pledging to restore the 1973 Constitution and not to support military rule.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Benazir Bhutto was assassinated on 27 December 2007 in:
explanation: She was killed after addressing an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The National Reconciliation Ordinance (2007) was declared void by the Supreme Court in:
explanation: In December 2009 the Supreme Court struck down the NRO, which had withdrawn cases against politicians and officials.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pervez Musharraf resigned as President in August 2008 while facing:
explanation: The new PPP-led coalition moved to impeach Musharraf, and he resigned on 18 August 2008.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who succeeded Pervez Musharraf as President in 2008?
explanation: Asif Ali Zardari, co-chairman of the PPP, was elected President in September 2008.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After the 2008 general elections, who was elected Prime Minister?
explanation: Yousaf Raza Gilani of the PPP was elected Prime Minister unopposed in March 2008.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Prime Minister was disqualified in 2012 after being convicted of contempt of court?
explanation: Gilani was convicted for refusing to write to Swiss authorities about cases against President Zardari and was held disqualified.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who replaced Yousaf Raza Gilani as Prime Minister in 2012?
explanation: Raja Pervaiz Ashraf led the PPP government until the Assembly completed its term in 2013.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 2013 general elections were significant because they produced:
o: The first election held on adult franchise
The first transfer of power from one elected government that completed its term to another
The first coalition government in Pakistan
The first election boycotted by all major parties
explanation: The PPP-led Assembly was the first to complete its five-year term and hand over to another elected government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who was the first person to become Prime Minister of Pakistan three times?
explanation: Nawaz Sharif became Prime Minister in 1990, 1997 and 2013; Benazir Bhutto held the office twice.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who was elected President of Pakistan in 2013?
explanation: PML-N nominee Mamnoon Hussain succeeded Asif Ali Zardari, the first elected President to complete a full term.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Prime Minister was disqualified by the Supreme Court in the Panama Papers case in 2017?
explanation: In July 2017 the Supreme Court disqualified Nawaz Sharif under Article 62(1)(f) for not declaring a receivable salary.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who replaced Nawaz Sharif as Prime Minister after his disqualification in 2017?
explanation: Shahid Khaqan Abbasi of the PML-N served as Prime Minister until the 2018 elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which party formed the federal government after the 2018 general elections?
explanation: The PTI emerged as the largest party, and Imran Khan was elected Prime Minister in August 2018.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who was elected President of Pakistan in 2018?
explanation: PTI's Arif Alvi defeated Maulana Fazlur Rehman and Aitzaz Ahsan in the presidential election of September 2018.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Pakistan Democratic Movement (PDM), formed in 2020, was an opposition alliance against the government of:
explanation: Opposition parties led by Maulana Fazlur Rehman formed the PDM in September 2020 to campaign against the PTI government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In April 2022, Imran Khan became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to be removed through:
explanation: The National Assembly passed a no-confidence resolution against Imran Khan in April 2022, the first such successful vote against a Prime Minister.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who was elected Prime Minister after Imran Khan's removal in April 2022?
explanation: Shehbaz Sharif, President of the PML-N, headed a coalition government from April 2022.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who served as caretaker Prime Minister before the general elections of February 2024?
explanation: Senator Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar headed the caretaker government from August 2023 until March 2024.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which politician was elected President of Pakistan for a second time in March 2024?
explanation: Asif Ali Zardari, President from 2008 to 2013, was elected again after the February 2024 elections.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under Article 50, the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) of Pakistan consists of:
o: The President and two Houses: the National Assembly and the Senate
The National Assembly and the Senate only
The National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies
The Senate, the National Assembly and the Cabinet
explanation: Article 50 makes the President a constituent part of Parliament along with the National Assembly and the Senate.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which House of Parliament cannot be dissolved?
explanation: The Senate is a continuing body whose members retire in turns, whereas the National Assembly can be dissolved before its term ends.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Members of the Senate are elected for a term of:
explanation: Senators serve six-year terms, with half of them retiring every three years.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Elections for half of the Senate seats are held every:
explanation: Staggered elections every three years keep the Senate continuous, since half its members always remain in office.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Senate provides each province with:
explanation: Equal provincial representation in the Senate balances the population-based National Assembly, where Punjab has most seats.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Senators representing the provinces are elected by:
o: Members of the respective Provincial Assemblies
The President on the advice of the Prime Minister
explanation: Each Provincial Assembly elects its province's senators through the single transferable vote.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Senate of Pakistan is presided over by the:
explanation: The Senate elects a Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among its members; the National Assembly is presided over by the Speaker.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The minimum age for election as a member of the Senate is:
explanation: A senator must be at least thirty, while a member of the National Assembly must be at least twenty-five.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The minimum age for election to the National Assembly is:
explanation: Article 62 requires a member of the National Assembly to be at least twenty-five years of age.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Unless dissolved earlier, the National Assembly continues for:
o: Five years from its first meeting
Six years from its first meeting
explanation: Article 52 fixes the National Assembly's term at five years from the day of its first meeting.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: A joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament is presided over by the:
explanation: Joint sittings, for example to consider bills on which the Houses disagree, are chaired by the Speaker of the National Assembly.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: If both the President and the Chairman of the Senate are unavailable, who acts as President?
o: The Speaker of the National Assembly
The Deputy Chairman of the Senate
explanation: Article 49 provides that the Speaker of the National Assembly performs the President's functions when the Chairman of the Senate is unable to.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: If the President does not dissolve the National Assembly on the Prime Minister's advice, it stands dissolved after:
explanation: Under Article 58(1), the Assembly stands dissolved at the expiry of forty-eight hours after the Prime Minister has so advised.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Public Accounts Committee of the National Assembly examines:
o: Audit reports of the Auditor-General on public spending
explanation: The PAC scrutinises how public money has been spent, on the basis of the Auditor-General's reports.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: By a convention established in 2008, the Public Accounts Committee of the National Assembly is chaired by:
o: The Leader of the Opposition or an opposition member
explanation: Under the Charter of Democracy, the PAC chair went to the opposition so that government spending would be examined independently.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The caretaker Prime Minister is appointed by the President in consultation with:
o: The Chief Justice and the Chief Election Commissioner
The outgoing Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition
explanation: Article 224-A provides for a caretaker Prime Minister agreed by the outgoing Prime Minister and Leader of the Opposition, with fallback to a committee and the ECP.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The principal seat of the Supreme Court of Pakistan is at:
explanation: Article 183 fixes the permanent seat of the Supreme Court at Islamabad, though it also sits at branch registries.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Chief Justice of Pakistan is appointed by the:
explanation: The President makes the formal appointment; since the 26th Amendment the name comes from a Special Parliamentary Committee.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Judges of the Supreme Court retire at the age of:
explanation: Supreme Court judges hold office until 65, while High Court judges retire at 62.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Judges of the High Courts retire at the age of:
explanation: Article 195 fixes the retirement age for High Court judges at sixty-two.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The number of judges of the Supreme Court is determined by:
explanation: Article 176 provides for a Chief Justice and as many other judges as Parliament may determine by law.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Before the 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's highest court was called the:
explanation: The Federal Court, inherited from the 1935 Act, was replaced by the Supreme Court under the 1956 Constitution.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first Chief Justice of Pakistan was:
explanation: Sir Abdul Rashid headed the Federal Court of Pakistan and is counted as the country's first Chief Justice; Muhammad Munir succeeded him in 1954.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: A judge of a superior court can be removed for misconduct only after an inquiry by the:
explanation: Article 209 empowers the Supreme Judicial Council to inquire into misconduct or incapacity of judges and recommend removal.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which High Court was given a constitutional basis by the 18th Amendment in 2010?
explanation: The 18th Amendment provided for a High Court for the Islamabad Capital Territory, which was then re-established.
